subject: Site Reliability Engineer — Observability & Internal Tools
paragraphs: I am applying for the Site Reliability Engineer role on Observability & Internal Tools. The description asks for the guardian and architect of internal infrastructure — someone who designs systems instead of consuming SaaS and owns the stack end to end. That is the only way I have ever run infrastructure: the fleet, the control plane, the monitoring and the runbooks in this repository are mine, and I can explain every one of them.

The platform is one flake declaring thirteen NixOS hosts. The wanted state lives in the repository, each machine pulls it, and nothing is hand-edited on the target — GitOps in substance rather than in product name. A task control plane is the single operator interface, git work runs through a forge's REST API, releases are one step from build to gate to activation, and rollback is a pointer to the previous generation. Security sits in that path rather than beside it: SOPS/age secrets per host, an in-house certificate authority with short-lived certificates, nftables default-deny, and a vulnerability practice built on CISA KEV data.

On observability I will be precise, because the role is precise about it. I wrote the telemetry layer myself: a sentinel records job status, generation age, disk pressure and PSI into a ledger every fifteen minutes and pages me on any state that is not ok; gatus checks the services that must answer; node_exporter is declared on a fleet host and exposes the standard host collector set on :9100. I have not operated a Prometheus server, Alertmanager or Grafana in production — my dashboards have been that ledger and plain HTML pages, and I reached for them because they answered questions a generic dashboard did not. Formal SLOs with error budgets are new to me; thresholds and paging on state are not.

What the role would get is a builder with low tolerance for toil: three years of turning repeated manual checks into gates, an operator who reads journald, cgroup counters and tcpdump before guessing, and someone who writes the documentation the next engineer needs at 02:00. I have not run a four-day week or a large platform team, and my scale is thirteen hosts, not a company's shared infrastructure — that is the step I want to make. I am in Germany, so the remote-first setup works without relocation; German is C1 and English is native.

My salary expectation is 80.000 to 85.000 EUR gross per year, and I can start immediately or by agreement. I would be glad to walk through the nixconfig repository in a first call: it is public, and every claim above is inspectable there.
